summary.headline: Khadim India Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR83.6 crores (vs INR93.8 crores) with PAT of just INR0.77 crores; FY27 target is ~INR400 crores at 14% EBITDA.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations declined to INR83.6 crores from INR93.8 crores a year earlier, with gross margin of 51.5%, EBITDA of INR11.9 crores (14.3% margin) and PAT of INR0.77 crores (0.9% margin). For FY26, revenue fell 12% to INR367.1 crores, EBITDA was INR49.1 crores (13.4%) and PAT INR3.1 crores. Management attributed the decline to store closures, lower primary sales to franchisees and deliberate inventory and creditor reduction, which cost an estimated INR10-15 crores of sales over the last two quarters. The company also completed the demerger of its distribution and manufacturing business into KSR Footwear Limited during the year.

segments.name: Retail (COCO and franchise network)
segments.commentary: Store count at 31 March 2026 was 851: 189 company-owned outlets and 662 franchise outlets across 23 states and 4 union territories. Around 60 stores were closed over the last two years; target steady state is about 200 COCO stores.

segments.name: British Walkers
segments.commentary: Grew 6% YoY in FY26, driven by men's formal and semi-formal footwear; new launches planned.

segments.name: TFM portfolio
segments.commentary: Grew 46% YoY in FY26, with traction in premium and semi-premium categories.

segments.name: Skechers (partnership)
segments.commentary: Recorded sequential growth in Q4; management plans higher volumes and wider store distribution in FY27.

segments.name: E-commerce (khadim.com)
segments.commentary: Contributed around 5% of sales in FY26; management expects a higher contribution in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of around INR400 crores, which management called achievable despite demand risks.
FY27 EBITDA margin target of around 14%.
Gross margin expected to improve by about 50 basis points to roughly 48-50% on new season ASPs and premium mix.
Every 5-10% revenue growth could add about 100-200 bps to EBITDA margin; PAT margin of 2-2.5% cited as achievable if sales grow.
Inventory to be rebuilt in Q1 FY27 and to a level sufficient for about INR400 crores of sales by end of first half FY27; no store closures expected beyond those already done.
Net debt target of INR110-115 crores post restructuring.
capex_capacity: Store rationalisation largely complete (about 60 closed over two years); new openings to be mainly franchise EBO and TFM formats, where the company invests only in stock, with COCO used at strategic high-revenue locations.
Target steady state of around 200 COCO stores.
Working capital limits largely unutilised; management expects EBO collections to fund cash flow.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 volume about 14 lakh pairs vs about 12 lakh pairs in Q3 FY26; revenue flat QoQ due to discounting.
Demand soft through FY26, with pressure in mass and value segments; April 2026 sales hit by state elections in Bengal and Assam.
Products priced above INR1,500 were about 15% of revenue; products below INR1,500 about 80-85% (as clarified on the call).
Premium products carry 2-3% higher gross margin than mass products and less discounting.
Raw material prices up about 20-25% since February 2026; company raised MRP by INR25-50 in retail, with more pressure in distribution than retail.
GST rate cut passed through on price, but management said demand did not rise and ASP fell somewhat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How can the company sustain a 14% EBITDA margin with revenue falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline came from store closures and lower franchise primary sales; revenue should hold around INR400 crores and EBITDA around 14% next year after cost cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Why has blended gross margin declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Price cuts on products under INR500 over the last 1-2 years; Q4 margin improved and FY27 ASP increases should keep gross margin at 48-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was inventory reduced sharply (about 40% YoY)?
qa_highlights.answer: A deliberate call to cut inventory days; some Q4 sales were lost, and the company cleared discounted stock and reduced creditors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue not recover in Q4 after inventory correction?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock replenishment ordered in Q4 arrives in Q1, so the benefit flows in one to two quarters; INR10-15 crores of sales lost over the last two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving from mass value to premium?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said Khadim remains a middle-class mass value brand and will add premium products such as British Walkers and Sharon as a blend.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payables fall from about INR196 crores to INR111 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly the demerger, since last year's figure included both entities; the rest came from deliberately reduced purchases and creditor payments in Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Revenue still well below FY25 levels; FY27 INR400 crore target depends on inventory rebuild and recovery in demand.
Raw material cost volatility (up 20-25% since February 2026), with pressure on gross margin.
Working capital and cash: cash fell sharply in FY26 (partly demerger transfer), and receivables from franchisees are to be corrected.
Athleisure is structurally limited by small store formats, so growth there is capped.
Skechers scale-up and e-commerce share (about 5%) remain unproven.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and somewhat defensive: management acknowledged a challenging demand environment and lost sales, but expressed confidence in a return to about INR400 crores revenue and 14% EBITDA in FY27, with limited quantitative backing on timing.
key_quotes: So with the revenue remaining at around INR400 crores, again, next year, -- we will remain steady at the EBITDA level of 14%.
Already, the inventory correction has been done. Now this year, we'll increase the inventory to the extent that is needed.
But still, I think INR400 crores target is an achievable target, and we will try to get it done.
